issues.body: Section 4.1 defines one indexed timestamp per COMMIT record and phase 2 requires TemporalIndex::as_of to agree with GenerationRing::as_of on their overlap. ChangeLog::record_commit records the destination generation of a transition, so the ring's initial generation has no commit record. For any t at or after that initial generation's published_at but before the first commit (or for a store with no commits), GenerationRing::as_of returns the initial generation while the proposed index has no qualifying entry and retained_min is undefined. The status table's claim that t >= retained_min means some retained record qualifies also does not cover this state.
issues.fix_hint: Specify a durable, timestamped baseline entry for the initial generation (and for each post-rebase lineage baseline where appropriate), or explicitly compose TemporalIndex resolution with a retained/base-backup anchor that carries the authoritative published_at. Define retained_min and HTTP behavior for an empty commit log, and add acceptance tests for no commits and timestamps between initial publication and the first commit.
issues.title: The initial published generation is absent from the temporal index

verdict.summary: Round 2 resolves the three prior major findings: lookup is now sequence-ordered with timestamp bounds used only for pruning, commit records are designed to use the generation publication clock with an explicit compatibility decision, and the HTTP horizon/future rules use retained_min and an indeterminate trimmed-history outcome. However, the durable index still cannot meet its stated overlap-equivalence contract because it indexes only change-log commit records: the ring's initial published generation has no commit record. Queries before the first commit (and stores with no commits) therefore have a valid GenerationRing::as_of answer but no TemporalIndex answer or retained_min. This new major completeness gap makes progress regressing under the required scale, despite the substantial correction of the earlier issues.
